intro: A fairly quiet day, dominated by AI shopping agents and who gets credit for the sale. Reddit feeds were rate-limited (429) again.

must_reads.title: Meta's Muse is coming to the UK, and affiliate pixels stay blind
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Meta's Muse shopping agent is heading to the UK, and Shopify says affiliate tracking pixels don't fire when Muse completes a sale on Meta. Another sign that sales started by a link can finish somewhere the link's tracking can't see.

must_reads.title: IAB blueprint asks who gets credit when AI shapes a sale
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: The IAB published a framework that splits sales into human-owned, AI-assisted and AI-executed. If brands adopt it, the last click stops being the only thing that counts, which changes how link-driven sales get credited.

must_reads.title: Google steers Chrome users to Gemini for product details and reviews
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Google is pushing Gemini in Chrome to summarise product pages and reviews in a side panel. The shopper's questions happen in Google's panel, not on the retailer's page, so more of the buying journey moves out of view.

must_reads.title: Amazon Ads drops page-based royalty estimates from Kindle authors' reports
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Amazon Ads removed the page-based royalty estimate from KDP authors' ad reports and now estimates royalties per 'qualified borrow', without saying how many pages qualify. Authors measuring ad payback will see different numbers.

must_reads.title: Does The Affiliate Model Survive Checkout Inside AI Mode And Gemini? – Ask An SEO
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Search Engine Journal asks whether the affiliate model survives when checkout happens inside Google's AI Mode and Gemini. It's the same question as Muse: what happens to the referral when the AI does the buying.
